Rationale: Table-stakes guardrail: blocking a shopper from reserving after an Uncertain verdict would destroy trust; near-zero effort because non-blocking is the default UX — this is the absence of a bad feature, not a new one.
Without size/colour granularity the verdict is too coarse to act on — affects almost all product queries; model is already designed at SKU+size level so incremental effort is low relative to impact.
Core user-facing output that every other story depends on; highest absolute impact but higher effort than S7/S5 because it requires full signal-API integration and UI build.
Most shoppers browse on mobile; a verdict that is hard to read on a small screen negates the AI work behind it; low effort because it is a UI and copy concern, not a backend change.
Transparency about signal age could build trust with sceptical shoppers; confidence is low — no user research confirms shoppers notice or act on freshness cues vs. just reading the verdict.
Key differentiator vs. all three competitors; converts an Uncertain verdict from a dead end into a completed journey; lower reach because it only fires on Uncertain verdicts (~30% of checks).
The engine that makes S1/S3/S5 trustworthy; low RICE because effort is very high (5 signal integrations + ML model) and confidence is 50% until signal data quality is validated in a pilot store.
Required reliability floor; reach is lower because degraded mode fires only on signal failure; must ship with the feature regardless of RICE rank — it is a launch gate, not an optional story.
Essential for long-term model accuracy but reach is tiny (store managers only); implement post-launch as part of an ops tooling track.
Critical for measuring feature success; reach of direct users (product analysts) is tiny; deliver as part of the data/BI track in parallel with feature launch, not gating it.
